Q1: Option A is the fix the job's own comment documents (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 3510-3511: "raise the shard count by editing the matrix list alone (job-index / job-total feed the step)"), and it was used before to go from 12 to 24 shards (lines 3517-3518). It keeps `timeout-minutes: 20` (line 3513), the job ID `tests-system-python`, the step name `System-Python test shard`, and the runner-interpreter coverage from #9233. It also keeps every assertion in `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py::SystemPythonJobTest` true: lines 154-164 only require the matrix to be `list(range(len(shards)))` and the step to use `strategy.job-index` / `strategy.job-total` with the `'NR % total == n'` split. The planner should extend `system-python-shard` from `[0..23]` to `[0..31]`, which is 32 shards. If time scales with the number of functions per shard, the worst shard drops from about 15m16s to about 11.5 minutes. The planner should also update the comment above the matrix to cite run 43412753795 (shard 11 at 15m16s of 20 minutes). The repo has no other reference that pins the shard count or the matrix job names: the only matches are `ci.yml` line 3519 and the contract test. The required gate stays the aggregate job, which needs `tests-system-python` as a whole (contract test lines 166-171), so the new matrix entries create no new required job name.

Option C was rejected because it fails `test_system_python_job_uses_the_runner_interpreter` and reverses #9233, which GITHUB FACTS show as closed (completed). Option B was rejected because it changes the step script and the contract assertions with no need, since a matrix-only change already works.
